Girl Scout Troop donates 800 books

Piedmont Post · October 7, 2026 · 1 min read

On Saturday, September 26, Girl Scout Troop 32605 gathered books for their book drive. More than 800 books were donated by the troop to Bananas, a local nonprofit in Oakland that serves low-income families.

The troop of 12 Girl Scouts advertised for over a month about collecting lightly used books for kids age 0 to 8. The troop’s collection of 800 books from Piedmont and Oakland residents surpassed the amount they collected last year by 200 books.

Completing the book drive helped the troop earn their Literacy Badge. Troop 32605 is a co-op troop led by parents Katy Bradford and Lauren Freeman this year. The troop puts its focus on community outreach and volunteerism, and different parents lead the monthly events.

The troop’s next community service project will collect warm clothes to give to the homeless this winter.
